content.title: Boston Marathon 2026: Kittery man in top 100. See Seacoast runners' times.
content.text: April 20, 2026Updated April 21, 2026, 9:36 p.m. ETBOSTON — Samuel Bradbury forgets how many times he has run the Boston Marathon, but he will always remember his finish at the 2026 race Monday, April 20.In a field with more than an expected 30,000 runners, Bradbury, who moved to Kittery, Maine, last summer, placed 64th overall in a time of 2 hours, 19 minutes, 7 seconds.Bradbury, 45, who was 63rd among all men, won the men's 40-45 age group, and he was the first of 90 registered runners from Seacoast New Hampshire and southern Maine to cross the finish line. It was also his personal best time."I put in the work, that's for sure, but you never really know how it's all going to come together on race day," said Bradbury, who improved over his 2025 time, when he finished 62nd overall last year in 2:22:23 when he was living in Amherst, New Hampshire. "I definitely surprised myself."How did Bradbury shatter his best Boston by more than 3 minutes?"I don't know, " he laughed. "I had a good playlist, a good mindset, and my body was ready, and made it happen."Bradbury, who believes this was either his 10th or 11th Boston Marathon, picked up running after college as "a fun thing to do.""(Running) keeps me sane, and I have a lot of fun with it," said Bradbury. "Seeing a couple people out on the course that I knew spontaneously gave me a nice little burst of energy. I had some family down there. Unfortunately, I did not see them, but they were with me in spirit."Matthew Daly, 43, of Eliot, Maine, who was the fastest Seacoast runner in 2025 with a time of 2:38:30, crossed the finish line this year in a time of 2:40.42.Winnacunnet coach turns in strong timeWinnacunnet High School cross country and track coach Cassie Kruse, a Hampton resident, finished in 03:06:21. It was Kruse's third fastest Boston time in six years."It was a beautiful day to run," Kruse said. "Great energy on the course. The highlight was seeing my family at mile 10 in Natick."York mother/daughter meet at finish lineKaren Fogg, 59, ran in her 18th consecutive Boston Marathon, this time joined by her daughter, Sydney Fogg. Karen Fogg finished in 3:33:52, while Sydney Fogg finished her first Boston in 3:16:10."Absolutely amazing," Karen Fogg said. "Sydney crushed it, and I felt so great and beat my time by 7 minutes from last year. The weather was perfect; could not have been better."More Seacoast runnersMany runners qualify by running for charities. They include York High School graduate Ashley Lomasney ran as part of the Dana Farber Cancer Institute marathon team in support of her family's history of cancer. Lomasney finished in a time of 04:44:55.Cooper Miller, 19, a 2025 graduate of St. Thomas Aquinas, was the youngest Seacoast runner for the second consecutive year. 03:44:08Sarah Polom, 30, 04:45:23OgunquitWilliam Troy, 63, 04:44:05Sharon Lokedi wins Boston Marathon women's division for second year in a rowSharon Lokedi, 32, of Kenya broke away at the end to win her second Boston Marathon title and a prize of $150,000.She finished with a time of 2 hours 18 minutes and 50 seconds.She held the lead for the last few miles of the race, creating a clear win for herself. Last year, she was battling it out neck and neck at the finish line.In 2024, she set the course record, finishing with a time of 2:17:22, greeted by her mom as she ran across the finish line. In 2023, she won a silver the Boston Marathon. She's also won the New York Marathon.-Katie LandeckJohn Korir defends Boston Marathon men's title in record timeAfter taking a dominating lead midway through the race, John Korir won the title of Boston Marathon champion for the second year in a row. And this time, he clinched the course record, winning him an extra $50,000 in prize money.He finished with a time of 2 hours 1 minute 52 seconds.The course record for the men is Geoffrey Mutai’s record time of 2 hours, 3 minutes and 2 seconds set in 2011.Korir, from Kenya, comes from a running family. His older brother, Wesley Korir, won the Boston Marathon in 2012.Winning the marathon comes with a prize purse of $150,000.-Katie LandeckEden Rainbow-Cooper wins 2nd women's wheelchair race titleEden Rainbow-Cooper, who won the Boston Marathon women's wheelchair division in 2024, reclaimed her title with another win in 2026. She will take home $15,000 in prize money after taking the lead early in the race.Her time was 1 hours 30 minutes and 51 seconds.Last year, the marathon athlete from the United Kingdom, finished just off the podium.-Katie LandeckMarcel Hugs wins Boston Marathon men's wheelchair for ninth timeThe favorite, Marcel Hug of Switzerland, defended his men's wheelchair title, earning his ninth Boston Marathon championship. He finished with a time of 1 hour 16 minutes.Hug previously won the title in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2021, 2023 and 2024, 2025. He is also the reigning course record holder with a 1:15:33 finish in 2024, which broke the previous course record he set in 2023.-Katie Landeck
